item.description:
Abstract
This study employs density functional theory with the Hubbard U correction (DFT + U) method to investigate how Pu incorporation into distinct sites (Gd or Zr) in Gd2Zr2O7 governs locally weberite-like disorder and subsequently influences Pu immobilization behavior. We reveal that incorporating Pu into Zr sites induces spontaneous 48f oxygen displacement toward vacant 8a sites, forming weberite-like local motifs characterized by 7-fold coordinated Pu. This structural disorder increases the oxygen positional parameter xO48f and elongates average Pu–O48f bonds. Solution energies confirm preferential Pu immobilization at Zr sites, where the locally disordered weberite-like arrangement provides additional stabilization. Electronic structure analysis reveals that Pu incorporation into Zr sites induces stronger Pu–O hybridization than Gd-site substitution. Crucially, the 7-coordinated Pu in locally disordered weberite-like arrangements exhibits pronounced ionic character, which could favor Pu immobilization at Zr sites in Gd2Zr2O7. These results suggest that local weberite-like disorder may be a key mechanism for optimizing Pu immobilization in pyrochlore ceramics.

item.title: 3D-Printed GelMA Microneedles with Multilayer Therapeutic Properties for Diabetic Wound-Relevant Drug Delivery
item.description:
Abstract
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic disease characterized by impaired insulin secretion, reduced insulin sensitivity, and hyperglycemia. Diabetic wounds are among the major complications of T2DM and can lead to chronic wounds due to challenges in the normal healing process. In this study, a three-layered tissue scaffold incorporating microneedles (MNs) was developed for diabetic wound management. The scaffold was fabricated using digital light processing (DLP) for the GelMA-based layers and electrohydrodynamic atomization (EHDA) for the surface coating, combining antibacterial, metabolic, and antioxidant functions within a single platform. The first two layers were designed using gelatin methacrylate (GelMA) and produced via DLP. The first layer was loaded with the antibiotic amoxicillin to prevent infection at the scaffold application site. In the second layer, MNs containing metformin were designed. For the outermost layer, polylactic acid (PLA) microparticles containing antioxidant and antibacterial salicylic acid (SA) were produced via the EHDA method and coated onto the scaffold surface. This three-layered scaffold was characterized by SEM, FT-IR, DSC, and mechanical, swelling, degradation, and penetration analyses. In vitro studies of single-drug-loaded model formulations demonstrated biphasic drug-release behavior over 72 h, effective antibacterial activity against E. coli and S. aureus, and favorable cytocompatibility. Oxidative-stress assays showed lower Total Oxidant Status (TOS) levels and higher Total Antioxidant Status (TAS) values in the drug-loaded formulations, while the scratch assay demonstrated increased wound-gap closure under hyperglycemic culture conditions. Overall, the multilayer microneedle platform exhibited antibacterial activity, with inhibition zones of up to 23 mm, and favorable cytocompatibility, with cell viability remaining above 77% across all formulations. These findings provide in vitro proof-of-concept evidence for the multifunctional design of the platform but do not demonstrate wound-healing efficacy in diabetic tissue.

item.title: Nanoimaging, Spectroscopy, and Biosensor Assays for Alternatively Spliced RNA Isoforms in Disease Diagnostics
item.description:
Abstract
Alternative splicing (AS) generates distinct mRNA isoforms, and frequently distinct proteins, from single genes; its dysregulation is established in cancer, neurodegeneration, and immune disease. Sequencing now nominates candidate splice events at scale, but a nominated event does not become a usable measurement until an isoform-discriminating sequence has been converted into a physical signal. Existing AS reviews concentrate on sequencing workflows, computational event calling, or disease catalogs; the assay-engineering step that follows target nomination remains comparatively underserved, and it is where most translational failures occur. This review addresses that gap. We group postsequencing detection into five classes defined by the physical origin of the signal: (i) fixed-tissue in situ localization, (ii) live-cell RNA imaging, (iii) plasmonic and spectroscopic readouts, (iv) label-free nanophotonic biosensing combined with site-specific RNA processing, and (v) protein-level proteogenomic confirmation. These classes are compared on target definition, reported analytical performance, multiplexing, matrix compatibility, perturbation risk, and clinical readiness. The reported performance spans single-copy imaging of splice variants in living cells to label-free detection at 580 fM in under 30 min without cDNA synthesis or PCR. Three conclusions follow. First, assay selection should be governed by the class of claim being made rather than by platform novelty. Second, analytical sensitivity measured on synthetic targets systematically overstates readiness in clinical matrices; therefore, matrix-matched validation is not optional. Third, cross-laboratory comparison is currently obstructed by inconsistent reporting, which we address by proposing a minimum performance-reporting set and explicit platform-selection criteria. We close with emerging directions, including CRISPR-based isoform detection, biosensor integration with nanopore sequencing, AI-assisted probe design, and digital and microfluidic formats.

item.title: Steric Scaling of Hydrogen Transport in FCC Transition Metals for Mechanically Consistent Molecular Dynamics Simulations
item.description:
Abstract
Hydrogen diffusion in face-centered cubic metals is examined using replicate-resolved molecular dynamics that quantifies temperature-dependent transport and lattice stability. Transport in Ni, Co and Pd is modeled with a hybrid embedded-atom method/Lennard-Jones framework at 800, 900, 1000, and 1250 K. Rather than fitting hydrogen–metal interactions to a single diffusivity, migration energetics are constrained through steric scaling of the FCC interstitial geometry. All baseline finite-concentration parametrizations remain structurally stable under the monitored lattice-volume criteria. Volume fluctuations stay below 0.15% and swelling below 0.09%. Late-time mean-squared displacement remains linear in all accepted trajectories. Four-temperature Arrhenius fits are stable for Ni, Co, and uniform Pd, while scaled Pd remains less constrained. The expected diffusivity hierarchy DPd > DCo ≈ DNi is recovered. Steric scaling lowers Pd diffusivity at every temperature while leaving Ni and Co unchanged, since their interaction parameters are fixed. Pathway-resolved single-H calculations give 0 K barriers of 0.1516 eV for Ni and 0.1294 eV for Co. For Pd, scaling raises the verified static barrier from 0.0234 to 0.0398 eV. A higher-loading Pd test retains the diffusivity reduction while lattice swelling remains bounded. Steric scaling therefore modulates the resolved migration landscape while preserving lattice stability and the observed finite-temperature diffusivity trends.

item.title: Dual-Kinetic Relaxation Spectroscopy for Discrimination of Volatile Organic Mixtures via Finite-Size Surface Gratings
item.description:
Abstract
Discrimination of chemically similar volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in gas mixtures remains a challenge for traditional optical refractive index sensors. In this work, we used a surface holographic grating relaxation technique to monitor the transport kinetics of VOCs. By analyzing the decay of the diffraction efficiency, we extract two independent relaxation time constants. These constants arise from the interplay between the local diffusion of the gas molecules through the material and the geometric aperture losses of the sensing surface (diffusion of molecules in air underneath the grating sensor). These parameters provide a unique kinetic fingerprint for individual species. Mapping these values in a 2D inverse-time state space reveals distinct, nonoverlapping clusters. Furthermore, in the presence of multicomponent gas molecules, by mapping the relaxation lifetimes of pure volatiles and their binary mixtures, we identify a predictable transition in the state space. This approach enables the discrimination between individual volatile compounds and mixtures (e.g., methanol-ethanol) and, in principle, allows their respective concentrations to be quantified and monitored over time with a high degree of sensitivity. This dual-parameter approach uses the finite-size effects of the probe beam, traditionally considered an experimental limitation, to enhance sensor selectivity, offering a robust framework for miniaturizing complex gas-phase analysis.

item.title: Quantification of Partial Oxidation of Magnetite to Maghemite in Aqueous Solution Using XRD
item.description:
Abstract
In aqueous solutions, magnetite (Fe3O4) nanoparticles (NPs) easily oxidize into a material with crystalline characteristics in between magnetite and maghemite (γ-Fe2O3), inevitably modifying their properties. The routine quantification and characterization of this transformation were previously hampered by the structural similarity of magnetite and maghemite. Here, we compared X-ray Absorption Fine Structure (XAFS) characterization to laboratory-based X-ray Diffraction (XRD) pattern analysis, such as Rietveld refinement and peak position shifts of the (311), (400), (511), and (440) reflections, to determine if XRD can be used to determine magnetite oxidation by itself. We analyzed the transformation extent of nanoparticles (10 nm) reacting under different concentrations of oxidizing agents such as O2 and H2O2. We showed that XRD methods─Rietveld refinements and single peak, such as (511)-based─can within error reproduce XAFS results. Our results document a more accessible characterization method for the quantification of magnetite NPs partial oxidation in solution.

item.title: Waterborne Hydrophobic Hard Coatings Based on Fluorinated Silica with Maintained Optical Transparency for Automotive Display Films
item.description:
Abstract
A waterborne fluorinated silica nanoemulsion was developed as a multifunctional additive for transparent automotive display coatings. Aqueous colloidal silica was first functionalized with γ-methacryloxypropyltrimethoxysilane (γ-MPS), followed by KPS-initiated polymerization of dodecafluoroheptyl methacrylate (DFMA). The modified silica was blended with a waterborne acrylate emulsion and wet-coated onto PC/PMMA films. Solid-state 29Si NMR confirmed γ-MPS condensation through the formation of T2 and T3 species, while XPS verified the introduction of DFMA-derived fluorinated groups. The optimized coating exhibited a water contact angle of approximately 107°, pencil hardness up to 3H, and visible-light transmittance of about 90% or higher. Fingerprint contamination and wiping tests further demonstrated improved easy-clean performance; the haze of the coated film decreased to approximately 0.99% after only two wiping steps, compared with 1.52% for bare PC/PMMA under the same conditions. After 100 steel-wool abrasion cycles, the transmittance change was limited to 0.4%, compared with 0.9% for the unfilled acrylic coating and 2.7% for bare PC/PMMA. SEM analysis confirmed reduced scratching and surface deformation. These results demonstrate a promising waterborne route to transparent, hydrophobic, easy-clean, and abrasion-resistant coatings for automotive display applications.

item.title: Presowing Management as a Factor Influencing Vegetative, Reproductive, and Biochemical Performance in Soybean Seed Production
item.description:
Abstract
Although chemical, biological, and vitamin-based seed treatments are individually well documented in soybean, comparative evidence on their combined application within a single experimental framework remains scarce. This study evaluated the effects of treating soybean seeds with a chemical product, Azospirillum spp. (2 mL kg–1 of seed), and the B-complex vitamins pyridoxine (B6) and nicotinamide (B3) (100 mg kg–1 of seed), applied alone and in combination, on gas exchange, vegetative growth, reproductive performance, and seed biochemical composition of soybean grown under greenhouse conditions. Seed treatments altered intercellular CO2 concentration and increased carboxylation efficiency, without significantly affecting net photosynthesis, stomatal conductance, transpiration, or water use efficiency. Treated plants showed greater plant height, branching, and pod number, together with higher seed number and mass, with Azospirillum spp producing the most consistent gains. Protein, lipid, amino acid, and soluble sugar contents increased with seed treatment, while proline remained unchanged, indicating a beneficial physiological stimulus rather than a stress response. These findings show that combining chemical, biological, and vitamin-based seed treatments improves vigor and early performance in soybean seed production and provide a practical basis for developing multi-input seed treatment protocols, although validation under field conditions is still required.

item.title: Optimization and Application of ReaxFF for the Aqueous Carbonation of Calcium Silicates in Steel Slag
item.description:
Abstract
The existing ReaxFF for the C/H/O/Ca/Si system exhibits poor compatibility with aqueous multiphase reactions. In this work, the aqueous carbonation of dicalcium silicate (C2S) derived from steel slag was selected as the research system, and parameter optimization and validation of the reactive force field were performed. Density functional theory with the GGA-PBE functional was adopted to conduct structural relaxation and potential energy surface scanning for C2S polymorphs, carbonate species, and reaction intermediates, and a comprehensive structure-energy training data set was established. Subsequently, ReaxFF parameters were trained using the ParAMS module, and molecular dynamics simulations of aqueous C2S carbonation were implemented via the LAMMPS code. The results show that the equation-of-state curves (volume-energy, bond length-energy, etc.) of the optimized C/H/O/Ca/Si force field agree well with the DFT reference data, which effectively addresses the difficulty in characterizing multiphase interfacial reactions involving water molecules. This optimized force field was applied to 10 ns MD simulations for the aqueous carbonation of β-C2S and γ-C2S. The simulations successfully reproduced the efficient adsorption and accumulation of CO2 and H2O on the C2S surface, while maintaining favorable computational efficiency with conventional computing resources. The force field parameters obtained in this study provide a robust computational tool for further elucidating the microscopic mechanism of aqueous carbon sequestration by calcium silicates.

item.title: Structure–Property Relationships of PAM/CMC-Based Semi-IPN Hydrogels: Influence of APS/ANI Ratio on Swelling, Electrical, Thermal, and Morphological Properties
item.description:
Abstract
In this work, semi-interpenetrating network (semi-IPN) hydrogels based on polyacrylamide (PAM)/CMC matrices incorporating polyaniline (PANI) were synthesized to investigate the influence of the ammonium persulfate/aniline (APS/ANI) ratio on structure–property relationships. Hydrogels were prepared via free radical polymerization of PAM/CMC followed by in situ polymerization of aniline within the preformed matrix, yielding composites with systematically varied APS/ANI ratios. Swelling studies in 1.0 mol L–1 HCl revealed that the incorporation of PANI reduced the equilibrium electrolyte swelling degree relative to PAM/CMC hydrogels, yet promoted specific ionic interactions with Cl– ions, strongly dependent on the oxidant/monomer ratio. Electrical conductivity analysis reached values up to 10–2 S·cm–1, with the highest performance observed for hydrogels synthesized at intermediate APS/ANI ratios. Morphological (SEM/EDX) and structural (FTIR, UV–Vis, XRD) analyses demonstrated that PANI formed dendritic-like microstructures distributed within the CMC-containing matrix, while XRD results correlated crystallinity variations with electrical performance. Thermal analysis (TGA) indicated differences in the thermal degradation behavior of the composites compared with the PAM/CMC matrix. These findings highlight the central role of the APS/ANI ratio in modulating the swelling, structural organization, and electroactive properties of PAM/CMC/PANI semi-IPN hydrogels, providing insights for the design of polysaccharide-based conductive materials with potential applications in electroactive devices.

item.title: Genetically Expanded Fluorescent SSB T7 RNA Polymerase in Action: Intriguing Photophysics with Enhanced RNA Production
item.description:
Abstract
T7 RNA polymerase (T7-RNAP) is a highly efficient transcriptional enzyme. However, it is prone to mutation at the functionally important Y571 residue, which strongly influences its functional properties. Here, we demonstrate a strategy to modulate the T7-RNAP enzyme by replacing the Y571 residue with a fluorescent triazolyl unnatural amino acid (FTUAA), TCNBAlaAc, via genetic code expansion (GCE) technology using two orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs. Thus, TCNBAlaAc-encoded variants, herein termed SSBT7-RNAP, were successfully expressed, purified, and characterized by SDS-PAGE, MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry, CD, UV–vis, and fluorescence spectroscopy. Incorporation of TCNBAlaAc introduced distinct and enhanced fluorescence signatures while largely preserving the overall secondary structures of the engineered enzymes. Notably, these novel TCNBAlaAc-encoded variants exhibited higher relative RNA yields than those of wild-type T7-RNAP under identical in vitro transcription conditions. Molecular docking further supported the structural compatibility of the modification with the promoter-bound enzyme. These findings establish GCE-based, site-specific incorporation of an FTUAA into a functionally relevant site of T7 RNA polymerase as a promising strategy for generating spectroscopically traceable, transcriptionally competent T7-RNAP variants for future enzyme engineering and mechanistic studies.

item.title: Temperature-Dependent Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance in Gallium Nanoparticles
item.description:
Abstract
The plasmonic characteristics of gallium nanoparticles of varying sizes were explored, with a particular focus on a novel nanometallic form of gallium. We investigate the temperature-dependent plasmonic response of these particles, revealing a unique behavior: gallium nanoparticles lose their plasmonic resonance upon heating and cooling. This reversible plasmonic modulation is accompanied by notable phase stability across a wide temperature range and resistance to ambient air exposure. Our findings highlight the spectral tunability and robustness of gallium-based plasmonic systems, suggesting their strong potential for integration into next-generation nanoscale devices and applications, where dynamic thermal control is advantageous.

item.title: Intramolecular Long-Range Photoinduced Electron Transfer Using π-Way of a Step-π-Conjugated Polymer
item.description:
Abstract
Photoinduced electron transfer (PET) along a π-scaffold with breaks remains poorly understood. To address this, we showed that a step-π-conjugated polymer (SPP)─made of alternating pyrrole rings and a single sp3 carbon─enables fast PET through its backbone. In this system, fluorescence quenching occurred when a perylene (Pe) donor was photoexcited in the presence of an anthraquinone (AQ) acceptor. To clarify the quenching mechanism, we considered four possibilities: (i) long-range (pseudo) through-bond PET, (ii) intermolecular through-space PET, (iii) short-range PET (through-space and through-bond), and (iv) intramolecular through-space PET. To systematically test which process dominated, we synthesized three polymers: water-soluble SPP, amphiphilic SPP, and poly(methacrylic acid) sodium salt (PMANa), which lacks π-conjugation. The fluorescence data of these polymers indicate that long-range (pseudo) through-bond PET is the main mechanism in the SPP system. Moreover, femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy reveals a Pe radical cation (Pe•+) and AQ radical anion (AQ•–), confirming charge separation through the step-π-conjugated backbone. The PET (kET) and charge recombination (kCR) rate constants for RDA ≈ 1.8 nm are estimated to be kET > 2 × 1012 s–1 and kCR ≈ 1011 s–1 order, respectively. Thus, SPP enables long-range, fast PFT via a new π-way mechanism.

item.title: Multifunctional CNF-Based Composite with Photochromic and Upconversion Luminescence Properties for Advanced Anticounterfeiting Applications
item.description:
Abstract
The development of advanced security materials with multimodal optical responses is of increasing relevance for anticounterfeiting technologies. In this study, we report the successful synthesis and comprehensive characterization of a multifunctional composite based on cellulose nanofibrils (CNFs) covalently functionalized with photochromic PSPA oligomers and cross-linked with upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs). Covalent grafting of PSPA onto the CNF backbone was done via Cu0-mediated radical polymerization (SET-LRP) and confirmed by spectroscopic analyses, while microscopic and structural investigations verified the homogeneous incorporation of UCNPs within the nanofibril-based hybrid gel. The resulting material combines reversible photochromic behavior under ultraviolet irradiation with near-infrared (NIR)-to-visible upconversion luminescence, enabling dual-mode optical signaling. The nanocomposite exhibited distinct and reproducible color changes upon UV exposure and characteristic luminescent emission under NIR excitation, demonstrating its suitability for advanced anticounterfeiting applications. Furthermore, the formulation as a stable, printable gel underscores its practical processability and compatibility with scalable anticounterfeiting technologies. The integration of photochromic and upconversion optical functionalities within a renewable CNF-based platform provides a robust, versatile, and sustainable approach for secure labeling and product authentication.

item.title: Optimizing Extraction of Bioactive Compounds from Grape Pomace to Produce an Eco-Friendly Smart Straw
item.description:
Abstract
Grape pomace (GP) is a byproduct rich in bioactive compounds. This study optimized the extraction of these compounds using a Central Composite Rotational Design (CCRD 22), evaluating temperature (41–69 °C) and time (0.8–3.2 h). The optimized extract (GPE) showed high phenolic content (163.99 mg GAE/L), anthocyanins (136.46 mg C3GE/L), and antioxidant activity (69.21% DPPH). GPE was incorporated into babassu mesocarp starch (BS) films, producing an active smart film (GPE-BS) that changed color at extreme pH (2 and 13). The GPE-BS film also showed improved hydrophobicity, antioxidant activity, and elongation at break compared to BS films (control). When tested as a straw for sugar-free cola, the film maintained structural integrity for 2 h. Thus, GPE-BS films are promising for smart food packaging or as edible straws.

item.title: Study on the Photothermal Performance Enhancement of Direct Absorption Solar Collectors by Heat-Transfer-Oil-Based MWCNT-TiN Composite Nanofluids
item.description:
Abstract
To improve the volumetric solar absorption capability of the working fluid in direct absorption solar collectors (DASC) and to extend its application to medium- and high-temperature solar-thermal utilization, mono multiwalled carbon nanotube (MWCNT) nanofluids and MWCNT-TiN hybrid nanofluids were prepared using Therminol 66 heat-transfer oil as the base fluid by a two-step method. Unlike previous MWCNT-TiN studies mainly based on aqueous systems, this work introduces the hybrid absorber into a low-polarity heat-transfer oil medium and employs oleic-acid-assisted dispersion and ultrasonication to improve particle dispersion in the oil phase. The optical and photothermal conversion performances of MWCNT nanofluids were first evaluated. The results show that the addition of MWCNTs substantially enhances solar absorption; the average transmittance of the nanofluid decreased from 68.43% for the base fluid to 33.44%, and the maximum apparent photothermal conversion efficiency reached 82.51% at 10 ppm MWCNT. TiN nanoparticles were then introduced into the optimized MWCNT nanofluid to prepare MWCNT-TiN hybrid nanofluids. The hybrid nanofluids exhibited further enhanced absorption in the visible–near-infrared range. At a TiN concentration of 10 ppm, the MWCNT-TiN hybrid nanofluid achieved the highest apparent efficiency of approximately 88.48%, which was 5.97 percentage points higher than that of the 10 ppm MWCNT nanofluid. This enhancement is mainly attributed to the strengthened broadband absorption in the visible–near-infrared region after TiN incorporation; this behavior is consistent with the reported plasmonic absorption characteristics of TiN, although the efficiency improvement is not attributed solely to a single LSPR mechanism. Supplementary stability evaluation of the optimized 10 ppm MWCNT–10 ppm TiN nanofluid showed that the UV–vis absorbance retention after 10 and 20 thermal cycles was approximately 98.0% and 95.5%, respectively. The particle-size distribution showed a Z-average of 66.533 nm, a PDI of 0.125, and a main peak at 75.529 nm, indicating good short-term optical and dispersion stability. This study provides a reference for the selection and application of oil-based hybrid nanofluids in medium- and high-temperature DASC systems.

item.title: Carbide Slag-Assisted Steam Gasification of Sewage Sludge for Hydrogen-Rich Syngas Production and Heavy Metal Stabilization
item.description:
Abstract
Carbide slag (CS), a Ca-rich industrial residue, was investigated as a calcium source for enhancing steam gasification of sewage sludge (SS) and mitigating heavy metal risks in bottom residues. Gasification performance and heavy-metal behavior across Ca/C ratios and temperatures were assessed using apparent retention, Community Bureau of Reference (BCR) sequential extraction, the toxicity characteristic leaching procedure (TCLP), and the risk assessment code (RAC). At 700 °C, increasing Ca/C from 0 to 0.75 raised the H2 volume fraction from 57.73 to 68.02 vol %, H2 yield from 207.40 to 332.85 mL g–1, and cold gas efficiency from 28.09 to 42.24%. CS addition increased the apparent retention of Zn, Pb, and Cd and was accompanied by redistribution from the F1/F2 fractions toward the F3/F4 fractions and by lower TCLP leaching concentrations; the RAC risk levels of Zn and Cd decreased from high to medium. However, CS was largely ineffective for As immobilization because its apparent retention, BCR fraction distribution, and TCLP leaching behavior changed only slightly, while As remained at medium RAC risk. At Ca/C = 0.50, increasing temperature from 650 to 800 °C increased H2 yield and cold gas efficiency but decreased the H2 volume fraction and H2/CO ratio. Higher temperature reduced the potential mobility and TCLP leachability of metals retained in the collected bottom residues but decreased the apparent retention of Zn, Pb, Cd, and As. Overall, under the investigated conditions, Ca/C = 0.50 and 700–750 °C provided a representative compromise between hydrogen-rich gas production, CS dosage, operating-temperature requirements, and the environmental response of the collected bottom residues.

item.title: Degradation Behavior of NBR Seals Exposed to Halogenated Olefins under Coupled Thermal and Mechanical Loads: A Multiscale Experimental and Computational Study
item.description:
Abstract
Halogenated olefins are promising low-GWP substitutes for traditional halocarbons in refrigeration, fire protection, and energy storage, but their compatibility with elastomeric seals poses a potential safety risk in process systems. This study systematically investigates the degradation behavior of nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) exposed to five representative halogenated olefins-namely, 2-bromo-3,3,3-trifluoropropene (2-BTP), 2-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropene (R1233xf), 2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234yf), cis-1,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234ze(Z)), and trans-1,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234ze(E))-under simulated service conditions (0–70 °C, 0–2000 N compressive load, 15–45 days). Overall, the performance evolution of NBR exhibits a strong dependence on environmental conditions, and is closely correlated with the molecular architecture of halogenated olefins. 2-BTP caused the most severe damage (compression set: 31.18%; hardness loss: 14.38%; compressive strength loss: 41.35%), while fluorinated olefins showed weaker effects. Microscopic and spectroscopic analyses confirmed surface roughening, microcracking, halogen penetration, and formation of C–X (X = F, Cl, Br) bonds. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that thermal energy weakens intermolecular interactions, whereas compressive stress induces chain orientation and free-volume redistribution, synergistically enhancing diffusion. The diffusion coefficients follow R1234ze(E) > R1234yf > R1234ze(Z) > R1233xf >2-BTP. Density functional theory calculations confirm that halogen radicals attack NBR’s C═C and −CN groups via low-barrier pathways. These findings elucidate the degradation mechanisms of NBR seals and provide practical engineering guidance for material selection and failure prevention, contributing to safer process design with halogenated olefins.

item.title: Multi-Isotope Signatures in Modern Pig Bones: Evaluating Dietary and Hydrological Controls on Provenance in South Korea
item.description:
Abstract
Multi-isotope analysis of animal tissues is a powerful tool for provenance studies; however, its application to modern livestock is complicated by the widespread use of manufactured feed and managed water sources. In this study, we investigated the mechanisms by which dietary and hydrological isotope signals are incorporated into modern pig bone tissues and evaluated whether bone collagen (BC) and phosphate (BP) preserve interpretable provenance information. 87Sr/86Sr, δ13C, δ15N, and δ18O values were measured in pig bone, BC, and BP collected from 17 livestock farms across South Korea. Bone isotope compositions were compared with corresponding feed and groundwater values to assess the transfer of dietary and hydrological signals into skeletal tissues. Bone 87Sr/86Sr ratios ranged from 0.70991 to 0.72280 and largely overlapped with feed values (0.71009–0.71226), whereas groundwater values differed significantly from bone values (p < 0.0001), indicating that Sr incorporation was more strongly influenced by diet than by drinking water. However, the relative contributions of feed, groundwater and other sources were not quantified for source apportionment. δ13CBC values ranged from −17.6‰ to −13.4‰, and δ15NBC values ranged from 0.74‰ to 5.31‰. Both isotopic systems were significantly enriched relative to feed (p < 0.0001), with mean offsets of 1.69‰ and 1.72‰ for δ13C and δ15N, respectively. Both δ18OBC and δ18OBP were positively correlated with δ18OWater, although BP exhibited relatively stronger explanatory power (R2 = 0.61) than BC (R2 = 0.40). These results suggest that modern pig bones retain measurable dietary and hydrological isotope signals; however, the use of manufactured feed can possibly weaken or obscure local geological provenance signatures. Notably this study provides a multi-isotope baseline for pig farms in South Korea and highlights both the potential and limitations of skeletal isotope analysis for provenance investigations of modern livestock systems.

item.title: Experimental Study on Fracture Propagation and Seepage Variation Law under Alternating Injection Acid Fracturing Technology
item.description:
Abstract
This study targets the ultradeep, high-temperature, and high-pressure carbonate reservoirs in the Penglai Gas Area, Sichuan Basin. The existing acid fracturing technologies have ambiguous stimulation mechanisms and are difficult to regulate accurately. We conducted a series of physical experiments on the alternating injection of gelled acid and drag-reducing acid, aiming to optimize acid fracturing techniques and improve the reservoir stimulation performance. Dolomite cores collected from the Dengying formation were used as rock samples. With a true triaxial hydraulic fracturing simulation system, we designed four groups of alternating injection cycles and different mixing ratios of the gelled acid and drag-reducing acid. Combined with three-dimensional (3D) laser scanning technology to characterize the morphology of acid-etched fractures, parameters such as fracture roughness (JRC) and etching volume were quantitatively analyzed to explore the laws of fracture propagation, etching characteristics, and seepage variation under alternating injection conditions. The experimental results indicate that the second alternating cycle achieves the best acid etching and permeability improvement performance. By contrast, the fourth cycle produces insufficient etching and thus reduces the fluid flow capacity. The permeability enhancement capacity is the best when the ratio of gelled acid to drag-reducing acid is 7:3, and the excessive or insufficient proportion of gelled acid will reduce the etching heterogeneity and the permeability enhancement effect. Fracture morphology, etching degree, and JRC are the core factors determining seepage and permeability enhancement capacity. The tortuous (vertical + transverse) fracture has the optimal permeability enhancement potential, and the riverbed/groove etching morphology with a high JRC corresponds to higher seepage and permeability enhancement effects. This work clarifies the rules of fracture propagation and fluid flow evolution during alternating injection of acid fracturing. It provides experimental data and theoretical references for optimizing high-efficiency acid fracturing technologies for ultradeep carbonate reservoirs.

item.title: Interfacial Regulation of Hybrid Nanoparticles via Silane Modification and Corresponding Pore-Scale Flow Simulation
item.description:
Abstract
High-temperature and high-salinity porous reservoirs impose severe challenges on nanofluid-based enhanced oil recovery (EOR), mainly including poor colloidal stability, excessive particle retention, and limited deep migration. To tackle these limitations, silane coupling agent 3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane (KH560) was adopted to regulate the intermolecular interactions of hybrid nanoparticles (HNPs). Colloidal probe atomic force microscopy (AFM) and quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation (QCM-D) were combined to quantitatively characterize the short-range adhesion and long-range steric repulsion, as well as mineral interfacial adsorption behaviors of HNP/KH560 blended systems with varied mass ratios. The results demonstrate that the optimal HNP-to-KH560 mass ratio of 2:1 effectively suppresses short-range interfacial attraction and strengthens long-range steric repulsion. This yields rigid and uniform adsorbed layers, which contribute to wettability alteration and the reduction of oil–water interfacial tension. Pore-scale multiphysics simulation was further performed. All interfacial boundary-setting parameters, including wettability state, interfacial tension, and particle-deposition kinetics, were derived from AFM and QCM-D measurements on the optimized silane-modified HNP sample. Simulation results show that regulated intermolecular forces induce uniform particle adsorption, neutralize pore wettability, and mitigate pore blockage, suggesting potential sweep-efficiency gains under simulated pore-scale conditions. Different from pore-blocking microspheres and single silica nanofluids, this silane-modified HNP system achieves favorable EOR performance via synergistic interfacial modification and controllable particle deposition. A multiscale quantitative correlation is established between microscopic intermolecular interactions and pore-scale transport properties. This work provides fundamental guidance for designing high-performance nanofluids adapted to harsh subsurface porous media.

item.title: Pincer Nickel Metalloligands for the Stabilization of Alkali Metal Alkoxide Aggregates
item.description:
Abstract
The structural chemistry of alkali metal alkoxides remains challenging to elucidate because of their high reactivity and tendency to form ill-defined aggregates. Herein, we report two complementary pincer nickel platforms that serve as metalloligands to stabilize well-defined multinuclear aggregates of sodium and potassium alkoxides. The reaction of a POCOP–NiBr pincer complex with MeLi or NaOtBu led to unexpected double C–O bond cleavage of the pincer framework, generating anionic oxygen-rich fragments that assembled into a zwitterionic trinuclear lithium complex {(η3-allyl)Ni}2(μ,κP:κO-iPr2PO)4[Li3(Br)(κO-iPr2P(O)Me)] (1) and a hexanuclear sodium cluster {(η3-allyl)Ni}2(μ,κP:κO-iPr2PO)4[Na6(μ4-OtBu)2(μ-OtBu)2(μ-OtBuH)2] (2). In stark contrast, the unsymmetrical complex (κN,κC,κN′-NCN)NiBr (3) reacts with KOtBu to form a centrosymmetric trinickel species {(κN,κC,κN′-NCN:η4-Ar,η4-Ar)Ni(μ3-O)K2}2Ni(μ3-OtBu)4 (4) bridged by four KOtBu moieties, in which the NCN ligand framework remains intact. In 4, the central Ni adopts a distorted tetrahedral geometry coordinated by four oxygen atoms, while each potassium center completes its coordination sphere through three oxygen atoms and an η4-interaction with a pendant phenyl group, revealing a rare κK,κO bridging mode for KOtBu. Comprehensive single-crystal X-ray diffraction analyses confirm all structures. These results demonstrate the capacity of pincer nickel halides to stabilize otherwise elusive alkali metal alkoxide aggregates and provide new insights into the ligand-directed structural diversity of these important reagents.

item.title: Characterization and Application of Water Kefir-Derived Dextran as Coatings with Chitosan and Antagonistic Yeasts for Strawberry Preservation
item.description:
Abstract
This study developed alternative biobased coatings using dextrans extracted from household- and industrial-type water kefir grains (WKG) to extend the postharvest shelf life of perishable strawberries. Extracted dextrans were characterized for their structural, physicochemical, antioxidant, and antifungal properties, and the most promising exopolysaccharide was evaluated as a coating matrix alone or combined with chitosan and antagonistic yeasts under cold (4 °C) and ambient (25 °C) storage. Dextran extracted from household-type grain (D-WKS) exhibited significantly higher antioxidant activity across all three assays than dextran extracted from industrial-type grain (D-WKD) (57.40 vs 49.30% for DPPH, 60.70 vs 51.80% for ABTS, and 63.70 vs 56.60 μmol TE/L for FRAP). Furthermore, D-WKS displayed superior antifungal activity against eight postharvest mold pathogens, demonstrating larger inhibition zones (4.90–23.01 mm for D-WKS vs 1.43–13.54 mm for D-WKD) and lower minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values (0.1–100 mg/mL for D-WKS vs 1 to >100 mg/mL for D-WKD). Cold storage proved indispensable for quality preservation. Under cold storage, individual chitosan treatment was effective in limiting weight loss and maintaining fruit pH, °Brix, firmness, and chroma values. However, household-WKG dextran combined with chitosan (D-WKS+Cht) was the most effective in maintaining surface lightness (L), total phenolics, and redness (+a). Notably, after 10 days of storage at 4 °C, D-WKS alone most effectively suppressed disease severity (5.45%), infection ratio (9.09%), and enzymatic browning (ΔBI = 0.089) while achieving the highest sensory preference and consumer purchase intention. Overall, utilizing water kefir-derived dextran alone or in combination with chitosan under cold storage offers a promising and eco-friendly biocontrol strategy for strawberry preservation.

item.title: High-Pressure Carbon Dioxide Adsorption and Dynamic Breathing Behavior in a Flexible Zn 2 L 2 Metallosupramolecular Mesocate
item.description:
Abstract
A discrete M2L2 metallosupramolecular complex containing bis-bidentate pyridylimine Schiff base ligand (L), [Zn2(NCSe)4(L)2]·5MeOH (1), has been synthesized and characterized. The solid-state structure of 1 reveals a neutral double-strand dinuclear mesocate architecture, comprising two Zn(II) atoms in octahedral geometry that coordinate with two chelating ligands L positioned in a side-by-side arrangement. Complex 1 demonstrates stability in water and a variety of common organic solvents, maintaining a pH range from 3 to 13, and can endure temperatures up to 240 °C. The thermally activated 1 has been examined for CO2 adsorption at pressures up to 20 bar and temperatures ranging from 0 to 55 °C, showing notable CO2 adsorption characteristics affected by temperature-dependent sorption hysteresis. The binding mechanism of the CO2-mesocate complex 1 was examined via in situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) at pressures up to 20 bar and a temperature of 35 °C. Notably, Hirshfeld surface analysis is employed to visualize and quantify intermolecular interactions, aiding in the identification and examination of active sites for the CO2 molecule. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of a supramolecular CO2 adsorption approach, utilizing flexible and low-symmetry mesocate components. The development of advanced carbon capture materials for both low- and high-pressure applications may benefit from this potentially promising approach.

item.title: Toward More Cost-Effective Hydrogen Production: Magnetron-Sputtered Ni- and Co-Based CeO 2 Catalysts at Ultralow Metal Loading
item.description:
Abstract
A series of mono- and bimetallic Ni- and Co-based catalysts supported on nanocrystalline cerium oxide (CeO2) was prepared by magnetron sputtering with a total metal loading of only 0.2 wt % to investigate the influence of the deposition sequence on the ethanol steam reforming (ESR) reaction. Structural analyses by X-ray Diffraction (XRD) and Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy-Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (STEM-EDS) confirmed that the sputtering process produced highly dispersed metallic species without detectable crystalline domains, while maintaining the mesoporous structure of the CeO2 support. Among the catalysts, Ni–Co/CeO2, obtained by sequential deposition of Co followed by Ni, exhibited the lowest deactivation rate constant (kd = 9.93 × 10–3 h–1), highest stability, and H2 selectivity sustained over 28 h of reaction. Postreaction characterization by EDS mapping, Thermogravimetric Analysis-Derivative Thermogravimetry (TGA-DTG), and Raman spectroscopy revealed minimal coke deposition on Ni–Co/CeO2, whereas the Co–Ni and NiCo counterparts suffered from higher carbon accumulation and faster deactivation. These results demonstrate that the metal deposition order critically governs the catalytic performance and that magnetron sputtering enables precise surface control even at ultralow metal loadings, producing catalysts with remarkable activity, stability, and coke resistance. Thus, herein, we highlight that magnetron sputtering is a promising route for designing efficient and economically viable reforming catalysts, which opens perspectives for exploring electronic and interfacial effects at higher metal loadings.

item.title: Comparison of One-Dimensional and Quasi-Two-Dimensional Friction Models for Hydraulic Transient Response and Energy Dissipation in Viscoelastic Pipelines at Different Water Temperatures
item.description:
Abstract
In chemical process systems, high-density polyethylene (HDPE) piping is widely used for conveying thermally conditioned liquids because of its corrosion resistance and operational flexibility; however, its pronounced viscoelastic response during hydraulic transients can strongly affect pressure regulation, process safety, and pipeline integrity, particularly under temperature-varying operating conditions. The temperature-dependent evolution of viscoelastic parameters, the differences between transient-flow models, and the associated energy-dissipation mechanisms remain insufficiently clarified for chemical engineering applications. In this study, transient-flow experiments in HDPE pipes at 20–40 °C were combined with numerical simulations using a one-dimensional quasi-steady friction model and a quasi-2D (quasi-two-dimensional) friction model. The first-peak occurrence time remained nearly constant at 0.1179 ± 0.0129 s, while the later response, particularly the third peak, was progressively delayed. The identified effective creep-compliance parameters increased overall with temperature and exhibited finite model-conditional admissible ranges. Model-based energy decomposition indicated that the calculated temperature-induced increase in total dissipation was governed primarily by the viscoelastic term WP, whereas the calculated frictional term Df varied comparatively little; the kinetic–elastic energy-exchange process also became shorter at elevated temperatures. The quasi-two-dimensional model did not yield a uniformly lower pressure-history RMSE, but its radial resolution of axial velocity and near-wall shear revealed model-dependent Df/WP partitions that became pronounced at 35–40 °C. These findings clarify the coupled effects of temperature and viscoelasticity on transient flow in polymer process pipelines and provide a mechanistic basis for model selection, pressure-surge control, and the safe operation of chemical-engineering piping systems.

item.title: Typical Pore Characteristics of Nontectonic and Tectonic Low-Rank Lignite in Mining Areas and Their Influence on Gas Desorption
item.description:
Abstract
Pore characteristics determine the control mechanism of gas adsorption and desorption in the coal bodies. The fundamental investigation into microscopic pore structures and adsorption–desorption characteristics of long-flame coal represents necessary support for the safe mining of low-rank coal and the exploration and development of low-rank coalbed methane. The research aims to fully reflect the differences in pore and gas desorption characteristics between nontectonic and tectonic low-rank long-flame coal. To this end, experiments on pore characteristics and pore size distribution of nontectonic and tectonic low-rank long-flame coal were conducted, as well as comparative cross-experiments on gas desorption laws under different adsorption equilibrium pressures, different particle sizes, and diverse types of damage. The trend of mercury increment changes in coal bodies with various degrees of structure was analyzed; characteristic parameters of coal bodies including pore size, pore volume, and specific surface area (SSA) were explored; and differences in the gas desorption speed and amount of coal bodies with varying degrees of structure were compared. Additionally, the main factors influencing the gas desorption in the main pores of the coal body were quantitatively analyzed. The results show that compared with nontectonic coal, the porosity of tectonic coal decreases and the SSA increases. The pore diameters are mainly large pores and visible pores, which are over half of the pore volume, followed by micropores and small pores, exceeding one-third of the pore volume; the increment of mercury injection and pore volume shows six special turning points, and the overall trend in each interval intuitively presents a W-shaped change with three peaks; the cumulative gas desorption amount and initial gas desorption amount of nontectonic and tectonic low-rank caking coal decrease gradually as the adsorption equilibrium pressure drops and the coal sample particle size enlarges. The difference factor of the cumulative gas desorption amount of nontectonic and tectonic low-rank caking coal affected by the adsorption equilibrium pressure ranges from 2.44 to 2.93, with an average of 2.69, and the difference factor of the initial gas desorption amount ranges from 2.50 to 2.73, with an average of 2.60; the difference factors of the cumulative gas desorption amount of nontectonic and tectonic low-rank caking coal affected by the coal sample particle size ranges from 1.24 to 1.59, with an average of 1.41, and the difference factors of the initial gas desorption amount affected by the coal sample particle size ranges from 1.40 to 1.74, with an average of 1.56. The difference in the degree of gas desorption influencing factors of nontectonic and tectonic low-rank caking coal is that the adsorption equilibrium pressure is greater than the coal sample particle size. Research findings provide important technical support and theoretical foundation for the rational selection of gas extraction and prevention and control measures during the mining of low-grade long-flame coal in nontectonic and tectonic areas, in terms of proper division of the mining areas.

item.title: Metabolomics-Guided Bioactivity Evaluation of Disease-Resistant Hybrid Grape Canes for Cosmetic Valorization
item.description:
Abstract
Grape canes constitute a valuable source of diverse polyphenols with recognized cosmetic properties, whose composition varies according to genotype and environmental conditions. Because grapevine resistance to pathogens is partly mediated by the biosynthesis of polyphenolic phytoalexins, disease-resistant Euro-American interspecific hybrids constitute particularly promising candidates for the sustainable sourcing of high-value natural cosmetic ingredients. Semitargeted UPLC-DAD-MS/MS analysis enabled the identification and quantification of 66 metabolites in grape cane extracts obtained from 24 interspecific hybrids and three Vitis vinifera cultivars as reference, cultivated over two consecutive years. Metabolomics coupled with unsupervised multivariate analysis was employed to characterize polyphenolic variability across the hybrid collection, revealing greater phytochemical diversity in Euro-American hybrids compared to European varieties. Antioxidant capacity was assessed using Oxygen Radical Antioxidant Capacity, ABTS, DPPH, ferric-reducing antioxidant power, CUPRAC, and metal chelation assays, alongside antityrosinase activity evaluation to determine skin-brightening potential. Pairwise correlation analyses between individual polyphenols and bioactivities were conducted to identify the compounds most strongly associated with antioxidant and antityrosinase effects in these complex botanical matrices. Overall, integrated metabolomic and bioactivity profiling highlights the strong potential of disease-resistant hybrid grape cane resources for cosmetic valorization.

item.title: Tyrosinase–SWCNT Electrochemical Biosensor for Tyramine Detection: Experimental Development and Molecular Dynamics Insights
item.description:
Abstract
Tyramine (TYM) serves as a critical indicator of microbial spoilage and significant health risks at elevated concentrations. Herein, we report an integrated experimental and computational approach to develop a high-performance electrochemical biosensor for selective TYM detection. Tyrosinase (Tyro) was immobilized onto carboxylated single-walled carbon nanotube-modified screen-printed carbon electrodes (Tyro–COOH-SWCNT/SPCE) to construct a nanostructured bioelectrode. The resulting biosensor exhibits a detection limit of 1.15 × 10–6 M and a linear range from 9.98 × 10–6 to 1.08 × 10–4 M. Furthermore, the biosensor demonstrates high selectivity toward TYM, with minimal interference (<10%) from common biogenic amines, including histamine, putrescine, spermidine, and spermine. Practical applicability was validated using spiked chicken meat samples, achieving satisfactory recoveries between 89.10–108.59%. To provide a molecular-level interpretation of TYM recognition by Tyro, molecular dynamics simulations and molecular mechanics Poisson–Boltzmann surface area (MMPBSA) analysis was performed. The atomistic simulations of Tyro reveal a copper-stabilized binding pocket that accommodates TYM through predominantly hydrophobic interactions. Molecular mechanics Poisson–Boltzmann surface area (MMPBSA) analysis yields a favorable binding free energy (ΔG = −22.46 ± 2.26 kcal mol–1), while per-residue decomposition identifies key histidine and valine residues near the binuclear copper center as major contributors to binding. By integrating experimental electrochemical performance with atomistics insights into enzyme–substrate recognition, this study provides a mechanism-informed framework for understanding Tyro-based biosensing and demonstrates its potential for rapid, selective, and on-site monitoring of food spoilage.

item.title: DAPEG, a Modular Peptidomimetic Concept for Intracellular Delivery: Architecture, Trajectory, and Outlook in the Context of Peptidomimetic Transfection Reagents
item.description:
Abstract
Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) remain a leading nonviral strategy for the intracellular delivery of polynucleotides and folded proteins, but native α-peptide CPPs are constrained by proteolysis, dose-dependent cytotoxicity, and endosomal entrapment. Peptidomimetic redesign addresses these limitations by replacing the α-amino-acid backbone, repositioning side chains, or embedding polyethylene glycol structurally. In this Topical Review, we present DAPEG, sequence-defined oligomers of 2,3-diaminopropionic acid bearing pendant polyethylene glycol arms developed at the University of Gdańsk, as a case study of how a single modular building block can migrate across functional categories within one decade, from fluorogenic protease substrates (2016, 2020) through plasmid DNA transfection with nonlipidated guanidinylated oligomers (2021) and delivery of active enzymes in breast-derived cell lines (2024) to lipidated plasmid DNA transfection in HEK-293T spheroid cultures (2025). To contextualize the chemistry, we survey eight peptidomimetic architecture classes now used as transfection reagents (peptoids and lipitoids, stearylated arginine-rich CPPs, PepFects, charge-altering releasable transporters, α-peptide/β-peptoid hybrids, PEGtides, modular peptide-PEG-oligocation constructs, peptidomimetic-functionalized lipids). We then examine DAPEG architecture and chronology; propose a mechanistic model for how N-terminal acyl-chain length tunes the balance between nucleic-acid condensation, particle size, and uptake (nonmonotonic and dependent on stoichiometry: the palmitoylated C16 variant gave the highest observed activity at a charge ratio of 1.5:1 and the acetylated C2 variant at 3:1 and 9:1, with C6 and C10 reaching the leading group only at 9:1); and acknowledge the six principal evidence gaps in the current DAPEG record as priority directions: the absence of in vivo data, unmapped cellular entry and endosomal escape, uncharacterized behavior in serum, unprofiled immunogenicity, a narrow cargo scope, and the absence of independent replication.

item.title: Fe 2 O 3 –MgO–CuO@MWCNT Nanocomposite for Highly Sensitive Electrochemical Detection of l -Cysteine at Low Potential in Biological Samples
item.description:
Abstract
A Fe2O3–MgO–CuO composite integrated with multiwalled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) was employed to develop a platform for the indirect electrochemical detection of l-cysteine (l-CYS). The material was characterized by XRD, FTIR, SEM, EDS, and EIS, confirming the formation of a hybrid nanostructure. After optimization of the experimental parameters, the modified glassy carbon electrode exhibited a well-defined cathodic response at −0.25 V vs Ag/AgCl (saturated KCl). Although l-CYS undergoes electrochemical oxidation at positive potentials (approximately +0.25 V), quantitative analysis was based on the effect of the presence of l-CYS on the cathodic response of the modified electrode. The determination of the analyte was performed using linear sweep voltammetry, yielding two linear response ranges of 0.5–100 μmol L–1 (R2 = 0.992) and 100–1000 μmol L–1 (R2 = 0.996). The lowest detectable concentration of l-CYS with the Fe2O3–MgO–CuO@MWCNT/GCE electrode was 0.5 μmol L–1. The sensor exhibited high selectivity, excellent repeatability (RSD = 1.58%), and reproducibility (RSD = 1.82%). The sensor was evaluated for l-CYS determination in urine and breast milk samples, providing satisfactory recovery values.

item.title: A Study on Heterogeneous Composite Flooding Technology at the Zhenbei Oilfield
item.description:
Abstract
Following polymer flooding at the Zhenbei Oilfield, issues such as the scattered distribution of residual oil, increased reservoir heterogeneity, and deteriorating production performance under high water cut conditions have arisen. To address these issues, this paper employs a heterogeneous composite oil displacement system comprising microspheres, surfactants, and viscoelastic self-regulating agents. Through fundamental performance evaluations and core displacement experiments, parameters such as injection concentration, timing, volume, and slug formation were optimized to enhance oil displacement efficiency and improve reservoir mobilization. The optimal total injection volume for the heterogeneous system was determined to be 0.3 PV, with an optimal injection concentration of 0.3 wt %. The system was injected using a three-stage slug combination comprising 0.1 PV of microspheres, 0.1 PV of surfactant, and 0.1 PV of viscoelastic self-regulating agent. The ultimate recovery rate was increased by 27.41% compared with conventional water flooding. Based on these research findings, field pilot tests were conducted at the Zhenbei Oilfield. Daily oil production per well increased from 0.9 to 1.3 t, while the water cut decreased from 68.6 to 56.7%, achieving significant water control and oil production enhancement. This validated the system’s excellent practical value for field application.

item.title: Matrix Acidizing in Dolomitic Rocks: Wormhole Development and Injection Performance Analysis
item.description:
Abstract
Matrix acidizing is widely used to improve the productivity of carbonate reservoirs, particularly those with significant dolomitic content, which account for a substantial fraction of global hydrocarbon reserves. In this study, the pore volume to breakthrough (PVbt) behavior of a dolomitic rock was investigated during acidizing with 15 wt % HCl containing commercial additives, namely a corrosion inhibitor (0.5% v/v) and an emulsion preventer (0.2% v/v). Eight core flooding experiments were conducted at 60 °C under a confining pressure of 2000 psi, a backpressure of 1200 psi, and an axial stress of 500 psi, with injection flow rates ranging from 0.4 to 4.0 mL/min. The samples exhibited porosities from 13.99% to 14.94% and permeabilities between 0.28 and 2.47 mD. The PVbt curve followed the dissolution trend described by the Buijse and Glasbergen model, with an optimum PVbt of 2.03 at 2.0 mL/min, corresponding to the most efficient stimulation condition and the formation of a dominant wormhole requiring the minimum acid volume for breakthrough. X-ray microcomputed tomography images revealed three main dissolution patterns: face dissolution and/or conical wormholes at low flow rates, dominant wormholes with branched structures under optimal conditions, and highly branched wormhole networks at high flow rates. The results demonstrate the strong influence of dolomite dissolution kinetics on acidizing efficiency and highlight the importance of selecting an appropriate injection rate for the stimulation fluid under investigation. This study provides new insights into reactive transport and wormhole development in dolomitic rocks and supports the optimization of acid stimulation treatments in dolomitic carbonate reservoirs.

item.title: Enhancing Alkaline Biodiesel Transesterification Using Protic Ionic Liquid [DETA][Hx] as a Low-Concentration Additive
item.description:
Abstract
Protic ionic liquids (PILs) have emerged as cost-effective alternatives to aprotic ionic liquids in biodiesel production. In biphasic transesterification systems, the intrinsic immiscibility between methanol and oil phases represents an important limitation affecting reaction performance. In this context, the present study investigates the influence of diethylenetriammonium hexanoate ([DETA][Hx]) as a low-concentration physicochemical additive in conventional KOH-catalyzed soybean oil transesterification. A factorial experimental design was employed to evaluate the effects of ionic liquid concentration (0–3% w/w) and reaction time (30–60 min) on biodiesel yield. The results showed that low concentrations of [DETA][Hx] significantly affected process performance, increasing biodiesel yield by 5.1% and reaching a gravimetric biodiesel yield of 97.1%. Physicochemical analyses revealed changes in surface tension behavior in systems containing [DETA][Hx], which, together with the observed yield response, are consistent with a possible influence of the ionic liquid on physicochemical and interfacial interactions within the reaction medium. FT-IR analyses suggested that the ionic liquid structure remained preserved under the evaluated conditions, supporting the interpretation that [DETA][Hx] primarily influences the reaction medium through physicochemical interactions rather than through direct chemical participation in the transesterification reaction. Although direct transport-related measurements were beyond the scope of the present study, the observed behavior suggests that low concentrations of protic ionic liquids may influence phase interactions and reaction performance in alkaline biodiesel transesterification systems. Overall, the present work provides experimental evidence supporting the investigation of protic ionic liquids as low-concentration physicochemical additives for biodiesel production.

item.title: Boosting CO 2 Hydrogenation Activity by Carbon Coating over a Nickel Catalyst
item.description:
Abstract
Earth-abundant metal-based materials play a crucial role in catalyzing the production of sustainable chemicals and fuels, offering a cost-effective and scalable alternative to precious metals. Among earth-abundant metals, nickel-based catalysts show the biggest potential for industrial applications. Herein, a series of nickel-based catalysts was synthesized by thermal decomposition of Ni complexes over an alumina support under argon, thereby forming a thin carbon layer around the monodispersed nickel particles. By selecting a ligand, the particle size could be tuned (from 10 to 5 nm), and the C-layer structure could be modified by introducing dopants such as N. The solids obtained were used as catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation. The material in which Ni particles with a covering C-layer overperformed the “naked” Ni particles at low temperatures. This may be related to the smaller Ni particles obtained from complex decomposition and a synergistic effect between these carbon layers and the Ni particles.

item.title: Nickel-Catalyzed Thiolative Cyclization of Cyclic Enynones under Visible-Light Irradiation: An Easy Access to 9-Sulfenyl-2,3-dihydrophenanthren-4(1 H )-ones
item.description:
Abstract
An efficient nickel-catalyzed thiolative addition–cyclization of conjugated cyclic enynones for the synthesis of 9-sulfenyl-2,3-dihydrophenanthren-4(1H)-ones is described. The reaction proceeds through a nickel-catalyzed hydrothiolation of cyclic enynones, followed by visible-light-induced intramolecular cyclization. This protocol tolerates both aromatic and aliphatic thiols, affording sulfur-containing dihydrophenanthrenes in good to high yields. The synthetic utility of the method is further demonstrated by converting the obtained products into valuable phenanthrene derivatives.

item.title: [Graphical abstract added] A Hollow Spherical Hydrotalcite-Based Catalyst for One-Step Ethoxylation of Butyl Acetate to Oligo-Ethylene Glycol Butyl Ether Acetates
Effect of Scrap Configuration on the Tensile and Flexural Properties of Grinding-Free Recycled CF/PA6 Composites
item.description:
Abstract
The increasing demand for lightweight, high-performance materials in the automotive sector has driven the use of carbon fiber/polyamide 6 (CF/PA6) composites. This study proposes a grinding-free recycling route based on the reassembly of CF/PA6 composite cutouts into a controlled laminate configuration, followed by hot compression molding. Three configurations were investigated: S21 (two layers of 1 mm-thickness square cutouts), S13 (one layer of 3 mm-thickness square cutouts), and R21 (two layers of 1 mm-thickness rectangular cutouts), all containing 85 wt % CF/PA6 scraps and 15 wt % neat PA6 powder. The recycled laminates were characterized by ultrasonic inspection, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), acid digestion for volumetric fraction determination, tensile and flexural testing, and field-emission gun scanning electron microscopy (FEG-SEM) analyses. Ultrasonic inspection and acid digestion showed that the S13 configuration exhibited the highest structural homogeneity and the lowest void content. In contrast, S21 and R21 presented higher void fractions, as confirmed by ultrasonic maps, acid digestion results, and FEG-SEM observations. Despite the higher void content, S21 achieved the highest tensile strength, probably due to the more efficient stress distribution throughout the laminate. Fractographic analyses revealed good fiber–matrix interfacial adhesion, as well as typical aspects observed in the fracture surfaces of thermoplastic polymeric composites, including plastic deformation, fiber pullout, and matrix-rich regions. Overall, the results demonstrate that the proposed grinding-free recycling approach enables the reuse of CF/PA6 waste in multilayer architectures in applications that do not require high structural performance.

item.title: Graphene-Reinforced PE-RT Nanocomposites for Flexible Pipeline Barriers: Structure–Property–Performance and Aging
item.description:
Abstract
Polyethylene of raised temperature resistance (PE-RT Type II) is the preferred material for barrier layers in offshore flexible risers, yet its CO2 permeability and long-term stability under hydrocarbon exposure remain critical performance gaps. Here, PE-RT nanocomposites reinforced with four graphene-based fillers─graphene oxide (GO), reduced graphene oxide (rGO), vinyltrimethoxysilane-functionalized GO (GOS), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNP)─at 0.5–2.0 wt % were prepared by melt compounding and systematically characterized. Filler surface chemistry and structure were characterized by Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Raman spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM/EDS), revealing distinct structural and interfacial features among the graphene-based fillers. SEM provided qualitative information on filler morphology and microscale distribution, while Raman spectroscopy and XRD were used to characterize the structural features of the graphene-based fillers. Because nanoscale dispersion within the PE-RT matrix was not directly quantified by TEM, AFM, or other image-based methods, relationships between filler dispersion and functional performance are discussed as structure–property interpretations rather than direct measurements of nanoscale dispersion. GOS delivered the greatest CO2 barrier improvement, reducing the mean permeability by 56.5% at 1 wt % relative to neat PE-RT (2.13 ± 0.30 vs 4.90 ± 0.10 cm2 s–1 psi–1; Tukey HSD, p < 0.001). The Nielsen tortuosity model yielded an effective platelet aspect ratio of ≈570, consistent with efficient platelet-induced tortuosity. GNP exhibited the highest mean stiffness at 1 wt %, with an elastic modulus increase of approximately 50.8% relative to neat PE-RT. Six months of immersion aging in synthetic hydrocarbon oil (ISO 23936-1, 80 °C) produced formulation-dependent changes in thermal, surface, dimensional, and molar-mass-related properties. The graphene-containing nanocomposites showed lower swelling than neat PE-RT, while GOS exhibited comparatively stable GPC parameters over the aging period. These results demonstrate enhanced aging resistance, although the specific mechanisms responsible for this stabilization were not directly determined. GNP showed comparatively poorer CO2 barrier performance despite exhibiting the highest mean mechanical properties among the 1 wt % nanocomposites. These results establish quantitative structure–property–performance relationships and provide design guidelines for graphene-functionalized polyolefin barrier materials in demanding service environments.

item.title: Core–Shell Upconversion Platform Based on an Amino-Functionalized ZIF-8 with a Covalently Anchored Ruthenium Nitrosyl Complex for Controlled Release of Nitric Oxide in Biological Media
item.description:
Abstract
The development of nitric oxide (NO) donor agents capable of controlled NO release upon light irradiation in the biological window is relevant for phototherapies. The cis-[Ru(dc-bpy)2(SO3)(NO)]+ complex (dc-bpy = 2,2′-dicarboxybipyridine) is synthesized and anchored onto a NaYF4:Yb,Tm@ZIF-8-NH2 nanoplatform. The isolated complex presents high stability under basic conditions (pH 9) and an absorption band in the visible region up to 405 nm. A core–shell platform of upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) coated with ZIF-8 is synthesized and functionalized with amino groups (UCNP-ZIF-8-NH2). This material exhibits intense blue emission upon excitation by near-infrared (NIR) radiation at 980 nm within a biological window. After covalent anchoring, through amide bond between the amino groups of UCNP-ZIF-8-NH2 and the carboxylic acid groups of the RuNO complex, supported by Fourier transform spectrophotometry (FTIR) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analyses, the UCNP-RuNO composite releases NO under 980 nm irradiation. NO release is controlled by irradiation time, showing an increase from ca. 0.095 to 1.015 μmol L–1 between 30 and 180 min. These UCNP-RuNO systems show in vitro cell viability up to ca. 12 μg mL–1. These results support their use as platforms for NO release under NIR light, with optimization achievable by varying concentration, formulation, excitation intensity, and UCNP composition.

item.title: Discovery and Design of YTHDF2-Selective and Pan-YTHDF Inhibitors for m 6 A Binding by the YTH Aromatic Cage
item.description:
Abstract
Recognition of N6-methyl-adenosine (m6A) in the RNA sequences by the YT521-B homology domain-containing protein family paralogs 1–3 (YTHDF1–3) is a dominant layer of myriad cellular regulation. Dysregulated YTHDF paralog expression and activities have been reported in cancer, including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) in which YTHDF2 has been identified as a druggable dependency. Guided by structure-based in silico screening, we identified structurally related small-molecule compound families of promising YTHDF inhibitor compounds. Following in vitro screening, two hits, DT11 and DT15, emerged and were further examined. We identified DT11 as a YTHDF2-selective inhibitor of the YTH domain using proximity-based bead assays, microscale thermophoresis, molecular dynamics, and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. DT11 demonstrated 10–100-fold YTHDF2-selectivity (IC50: YTHDF2 16.6 μM; YTHDF1 185 μM; YTHDF3 1300 μM) in inhibiting m6A-RNA binding, whereas the pan-inhibitor DT15 effectively inhibited all the paralogs (IC50: YTHDF2 12.6 μM; YTHDF1 18.8 μM; YTHDF3 31 μM). In LN229 glioblastoma cells, DT11 reduced cell viability and showed relevant additive efficacy with the gold standard Temozolomide. DT15 blocked GBM cell invasion and scratch wound closure. Similar effects were observed after inhibition of the m6A writer METTL3 activity by STM2457. No such effects were observed with DT11. A minutely modified DT11 derivative, DT11-1, showed 10-fold increases in YTHDF2-selective m6A binding and LN229 cell viability inhibitory potencies. All the compounds produced high GBM preference over primary neurons and HEK293 cells in their effects. Our results further define pharmacological molecular comprehensions for paralog-dependent engagement of m6A in RNA by the aromatic cage for the selective modulation of YTHDF functions.

item.title: Study on the Density Enhancement of a Solids-Free, Potassium-Based Phosphate Kill Fluid by Cesium Formate and Its Molecular Dynamics Mechanism
item.description:
Abstract
In the development of high-temperature and high-pressure oil and gas reservoirs, high-density, solid-free, well-killing fluids are essential for well control operations. Traditional weighting agents suffer from insufficient density and high corrosivity. Potassium-based phosphates are widely employed owing to their low cost and low corrosivity, but their density is capped at around 1.8 g/cm3. Although cesium formate brine can achieve a density up to 2.3 g/cm3, its high cost makes it impractical for sole use. In this work, we formulated a high-density, solid-free, potassium-based phosphate killing fluid by mixing potassium-based phosphates with cesium formate and incorporating 2 wt % corrosion inhibitor R-51. The density and fundamental performances of the as-prepared fluid were experimentally evaluated. Meanwhile, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were performed to clarify the intrinsic mechanism behind the density enhancement by cesium formate. The results show that the maximum density of the optimized fluid reaches 1.913 g/cm3 at room temperature, which breaks the density limitation of conventional potassium-based phosphate killing fluids. The fluid possesses good thermal resistance up to 180 °C and stable rheological behaviors. It achieves a rolling recovery rate higher than 91% and a corrosion rate of 0.0184 mm/a, with the core permeability recovery rate over 85%. NMR T2 characterization confirms that the prepared fluid imposes no substantial damage to the dominant seepage pathways of rock cores. MD simulations showed that the addition of cesium formate disrupted the original hydrogen-bond network of bulk water and reduced the average number of water–water hydrogen bonds per water molecule. In addition, the coordination number of water molecules around phosphate increased, and more water molecules surrounded the phosphate groups through hydrogen bonding with the oxygen atoms in phosphate, forming a compact hydration shell. These features suggest that cesium formate promotes more efficient atomic packing throughout the solution, thereby increasing the solution density.

item.title: Synergistic Wetting Mechanisms of Mixed Surfactants at Different Mixing Ratios on Anthracite: Insights from Molecular Dynamics Simulations
item.description:
Abstract
Anthracite dust exhibits strong hydrophobicity due to its highly aromatic structure and limited oxygen-containing functional groups, which restricts spray wetting and dust suppression efficiency. In this study, a nonionic surfactant C15H27FO4 (COAD) and an anionic surfactant C18H36CHSO3Na(OCH2CH2)7 (FMES) were combined to improve anthracite wettability. The effects of surfactant concentration and COAD/FMES mixing ratio on wetting performance were systematically investigated through contact-angle and surface-tension measurements. The interfacial mechanisms were further elucidated using SEM, XPS, and molecular dynamics simulations. The results showed that anthracite wettability exhibited significant dependence on both surfactant concentration and mixing ratio. When the total surfactant concentration is 0.05 wt %, it tends to stabilize, and the S3 formulation (COAD: FMES = 1:3) exhibited the lowest contact angle of 20.90°. SEM observations indicated that surfactant treatment promoted particle aggregation and interparticle adhesion, while XPS results revealed a decrease in aromatic carbon content from 91.30% to 80.32% after S3 treatment, accompanied by increased aliphatic and phenolic/ether carbon fractions. Molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated that the enhanced wettability of S3 was attributed to stronger interfacial adsorption and hydration effects. The S3 system exhibited an adsorption-layer thickness of 28.15 Å, the highest RDF peak intensity (0.273) between hydrophilic groups and water molecules, and the lowest water diffusion coefficient (0.24 × 10–5 cm2/s), indicating enhanced interfacial water enrichment and confinement. Overall, the optimized COAD/FMES system improved anthracite wettability through synergistic surfactant adsorption, hydration interactions, and interfacial water regulation, providing theoretical guidance for the development of efficient coal-dust suppressants.

item.title: Immobilization of Aspergillus oryzae IPT-301 Cells with High Transfructosylation Activity on Polyurethane Sponge for Fructooligosaccharide Production in Batch Mode
item.description:
Abstract
A stable and active biocatalyst for fructooligosaccharide (FOS) production was synthesized by immobilizing A. oryzae IPT-301 cells on a polyurethane sponge (PS) during submerged cultivation. Comparisons between immobilized and cross-linked immobilized cells revealed similar biochemical properties. The highest cell concentration immobilized in PS (11.89 ± 2.29 g cells g support–1) was obtained after 32 h. Both biocatalysts performed optimally at 50 °C, pH 5.5, and 480.2 g L–1 sucrose, showing a Vmax of 3500 μmol g–1 min–1 and high selectivity for 1-kestose (28.23%). They exhibited a half-life of 300 min at 50 °C, retained 40% activity after 28 days of storage and 50% activity after 12 reaction cycles. FOS productivity reached 116 g L–1 h–1 with a 24% yield. Statistical analysis confirmed that cross-linking did not significantly influence performance. The results show that in situ immobilization on PS is a simple, efficient strategy for producing stable biocatalysts for FOS synthesis.

item.title: Surface Roughness of Asbestiform Fibers and Cleavage Fragments of Amphibole Minerals: Characterization and Importance for Toxicological Evaluation
item.description:
Abstract
Various types of elongate mineral particles have different characteristics that can impact their biological effects and should be considered during risk assessment. Recently, a lot of attention has been paid to the morphological habit of elongate mineral particles, including a classification for asbestiform fibers and nonasbestiform cleavage fragments. Differentiating particle characteristics by habit is essential for toxicology, in light of studies showing that asbestiform fibers are biologically active and carcinogenic, unlike nonasbestiform varieties that appear to be noncarcinogenic. In this study, Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) was utilized to determine the surface roughness of 26 elongate mineral particles, including 15 asbestiform samples and 11 from nonasbestiform types. It was determined that the mean surface roughness value SZ for asbestiform particles was 147.7 nm (StDev 83.2), and for nonasbestiform, was 339.1 nm (StDev 156.9). A Student’s t test for two groups is statistically significant: t = 4.03, p = 0.0005. Correlation analysis revealed that surface roughness has a moderate negative correlation with the fraction of long, thin particles which are longer than 5 μm and not thicker than 0.15 μm (EMPA) (R = 0.51, R2 = 0.26, P < 0.007).
